A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PixelDiT work. Their readable main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet and text-to-image experiments, architectural ablations, sampling analyses, and qualitative editing results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds ImageNet-512 evaluation, quantitative editing results, additional ablations, extended training, and negative experimental findings.

M1.justification: The proposed dual-level architecture, pixel-wise AdaLN, token compaction, text conditioning, and velocity-plus-REPA objective remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A. Appendix G reports alternative designs and prediction targets as unsuccessful experiments, without replacing components of the final method.

E1.justification: v2 reports evaluation on the 281-pair FlowEdit editing corpus, broadening coverage beyond v1's illustrated bicycle-to-motorcycle edit (Figure 1b; v2 Appendix D.2). This extends an existing editing task; the underlying ImageNet and text-to-image dataset coverage is retained.

E2.justification: FLUX-schnell is added alongside FLUX-dev in the 1024-resolution text-to-image comparison (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 4). The new ImageNet-512 comparison also includes Bao et al.'s U-ViT-H, absent from v1's comparisons. Most existing comparator families are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include ImageNet-512 fine-tuning for 530 epochs from a 320-epoch checkpoint, guidance 3.5 over [0.1, 1.0], and extended ImageNet-256 training to 800 epochs. Editing evaluation introduces SAM3 bounding boxes and background MSE/SSIM on 281 pairs. Table 1 also changes the reported EPG configuration from 583M parameters/800 epochs to 789M/600 epochs.

E4.justification: v2 adds REPA removal experiments, ImageNet-512 patch-size ablations, resolution/patch-size compute analysis, and training-duration studies (Tables 11, 13, 16-18). Appendix G adds qualitative experiments on conditioning, transforms, prediction targets, and architectural alternatives. Existing solver, guidance, depth-allocation, and compaction analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Added results continue the same point-estimate reporting practice; longer training and additional evaluation samples do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Retained 320-epoch ImageNet-256 gFID 1.61 and text-to-image scores are unchanged. New entries include ImageNet-512 gFID 1.81, 800-epoch ImageNet-256 gFID 1.54, and editing background MSE 0.001522/SSIM 0.8628, alongside new ablation and negative findings. EPG's Table 1 gFID changes from 2.04 to 1.81 under a different configuration, not a matched-setting improvement.

T1.justification: The main mathematical formulation remains unchanged. Appendix G adds mathematical specifications for experimental variants: DCT-basis modulation with an O(KC) versus O(P²C) parameter-count argument, and a stabilized clean-image-to-velocity mapping. These are limited additions; no theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central single-stage, dual-level PixelDiT contribution is retained. The abstract extends its performance claim to ImageNet-512, while the conclusion strengthens the description from closing much of the latent-space gap to image quality 'on par' with latent diffusion on class- and text-conditioned generation.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of REPA's regularizing role, conditioning trade-offs, and unsuccessful architectural choices. Appendix G explicitly qualifies its observations as not fully controlled; Appendix I adds loss-spike risks for deeper models and long training runs. The conclusion additionally attributes pixel-space difficulty to data/noise complexity and immature training recipes, expanding v1's architecture-centered explanation.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies code, pretrained-model, and project links. It also documents additional preprocessing, fine-tuning initialization and schedules, SAM3-based evaluation processing, and implementation choices such as fixed sinusoidal pixel embeddings and the x-prediction stability threshold. These substantially expand access and reproducibility information; the linked resources themselves were not accessed.

R1.justification: v2 adds 'All Are Worth Words: A ViT Backbone for Diffusion Models' and 'Analyzing and Improving the Training Dynamics of Diffusion Models.' Section 2 otherwise retains its research positioning, while the introduction drops its explicit description of 1024-resolution training as a breakthrough over prior pixel-space models.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction receive localized edits, the conclusion is rewritten, and an ablation summary is added. The appendix gains extended-training and failed-attempt sections, with corresponding subsection renumbering. Most existing method, related-work, and experimental prose and the main section order are retained.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with an ImageNet-512 sample grid (Figure 6) and tables covering its benchmark, REPA, patch size, editing preservation, compute scaling, and training duration (Tables 2, 11, 13-14, 16-18). The text-to-image table gains a FLUX-schnell row. Existing diagrams, plots, and appendix image galleries are retained, with relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps: the previously illustrated editing advantage receives a 281-pair quantitative evaluation, and REPA ablations and ImageNet-512 experiments strengthen component and scalability evidence. Failed-attempt reporting, explicit training-instability limitations, and access links improve transparency and reproducibility information. The stronger parity conclusion remains broader than the mixed benchmark results, and Appendix G is not fully controlled, but these qualifications do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support.
